Notes.Text:
This update for cadvisor fixes the following issues:

Changes in cadvisor:

- update vendor.tar to address:
  * bsc#1288588, CVE-2026-116591: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd:
    crafted ~27 KB two-block zstd frame makes DecodeAll and the
    streaming decoder panic

  * bsc#1288212, CVE-2026-78663: golang.org/x/net/http2: double
    flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams
Notes.Title: Details

Notes.Title: Terms of Use

Vulnerabilities.Description: compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to 1.20.2, the zstd DecodeAll and streaming decoder paths can panic when a crafted two-block frame reaches huff0.ReadTable with an FSE normalized count of 32768 that readNCount stores in int16 as -32768. The wrapped count allows buildDtable to retain stale fse.Scratch decode-table state from the prior block, and nextFast then derives an out-of-range state and indexes beyond the table instead of returning a decode error. Both blocks are required to preserve and then reuse the stale state, allowing untrusted zstd input to crash an application. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.
